messages:
kevin: hi all, second day here. quick set of questions: when do i use @channel vs @here vs just pinging a few folks? where do people put "FYI" links vs questions that need answers? also the release-bot keeps DMing me ":sweat_smile:"
marta (People Ops): welcome kevin! short rules: @channel = urgent for whole channel (use sparingly). @here = people online now (still noisy). Prefer direct pings to specific folks for non-urgent asks. For FYI links, post in the channel with a short TL;DR and use threads for Q&A.
gwen (Eng): +1 to thread-first. If you need attention from a team, post in the team channel and tag 2-3 people, e.g., "hey @gwen @tariq quick question about routing". For things that require async decision or context, create a short doc and paste the link as the root message. That keeps channels searchable.
kevin: makes sense. any shorthand on posting code/errors? i've seen different styles.
gwen (Eng): minimal repro in the root of the thread please. Example we prefer: ```Service: edge-proxy
Env: staging
Cmd: curl -v https://edge.local/health
Error: 502 Bad Gateway (trace id: abc123)``` Add expected result and steps you already tried.
samir (DevEx): bot noise tips: 1) In App Settings > Notifications, set CI/Release apps to "Only mentions". 2) Use `/digest subscribe nightly` to receive a single digest instead of per-event DMs. 3) for release-bot specifically `/release mute me` will stop release DMs.
digest-bot: Digest nightly summary subscribed for kevin at 07:00 local
kevin: sweet. when should i DM vs post in #eng-general? some folks post quick Qs in DM then repost the answer in channelis that expected?
marta (People Ops): good etiquette: if the answer is likely useful to others, post it in-channel and thread the original DM summary with "Posting answer here for visibility". If its private (pay or personal), keep in DM.
gwen (Eng): small extra: if you ping someone in DM and they ask to move it public, copy the question and your conversation into the channel with the person's OK. That helps future folks and reduces one-off solutions.
kevin: gotcha. final onewhat's the etiquette for using bookmarks/pinned items?
samir (DevEx): pin the doc or gist if it's the canonical thing people will need often. Use bookmarks for short-lived resources (meeting notes, deploy links). Add a 1-line description when pinning so folks know what it is.
release-bot: [release] canary v2.7.0 rolled to staging by gwen - 2026-03-22 09:15 UTC
kevin: thanks all! i'll avoid @channel unless it's urgent, put reproducible snippets in the root, and subscribe to the nightly digest. :thumbsup:
